changes: Scribe Mukuṭānanda: confidence lowered high→medium (form 'mukuṭa ānandanena' is corrupt, probably for mukuṭānandena; the catalogue reads Ānandamukuṭa)
Date: era NS kept, but it is not stated in the colophon; notes now say it was inferred from the weekday check (Jyeṣṭha śukla 11 ≈ Fri 15 June 1883) and the late Devanāgarī script
Notes: added the stray '3' after jyeṣṭhe and why the era was chosen

date.as_written: triambaraṃ śūnyamekagatābde jyeṣṭhe 3 site haritithau bhṛguvāsare ca

notes: Chronogram tri (3) ambara (0) śūnya (0) eka (1), read right to left, gives 1003. The colophon names no era; the catalogue gives 'SAM 1003'. NS is inferred: Jyeṣṭha śukla ekādaśī of NS 1003 falls around 15 June 1883, which my rough calculation makes a Friday (bhṛguvāsara), so it fits. VS 1003 (946 CE) is implausible for a Devanāgarī paper manuscript. The '3' after 'jyeṣṭhe' is unclear: it may be a solar day, or a misread punctuation mark or abbreviation. 'site' = śukla pakṣa; 'haritithi' = ekādaśī. The scribe's name is corrupt: 'mukuṭa ānandanena' probably stands for mukuṭānandena (Mukuṭānanda), but the catalogue gives Ānandamukuṭa ('Ānaṇdamukuṭa'). Devānanda, son of Daṇḍapāṇi, is the author of the text, not someone involved in this copy.
